 By BVM Sportsdesk, 11/13/2026 San Diego State faces New Mexico State Sunday at Frontwave Arena, looking to build momentum in its early-season schedule. The Aztecs lead the all-time series 5-3 and are navigating a major roster reset: they return just 20.3% of last season’s minutes and 14.5% of its scoring. Junior guard Latrell Davis has emerged as an early offensive bright spot.
 By the Numbers Sunday’s game tips off at 1 p.m. PT.
 SDSU leads the series 5-3, including a 73-69 overtime win in their 2014 NCAA Tournament meeting.
 Latrell Davis is averaging 23 points while shooting 62.5% from the field and 57.9% from 3-point range.
 The Aztecs return 984 minutes—20.3% of last season’s total—and 374 points, or 14.5% of their scoring.
 Yes, But SDSU has a strong historical record and a standout scorer, but its limited returning production means the team is still adjusting to a largely new roster.
 What's Next The Aztecs meet New Mexico State Sunday in the Compete 4 Cause Classic. The matchup will offer an early test of how quickly SDSU’s reworked roster can come together.
 Bottom Line SDSU’s history favors the Aztecs, but this season’s prospects will depend on turning early individual promise into consistent team play.
